name: camelCase
notes: - Renamed to `camel`.

name: castArray
notes:
- If the given value is an array, the array is shallow copied.
- We also have `castArrayIfExists` which is similar but null/undefined are returned as is.

name: clone
notes: - Unsure about the differences as of now. [Help wanted](https://github.com/radashi-org/radashi/issues/113).

name: cloneDeep
notes: - Ours accepts a custom strategy (similar to `cloneDeepWith`).

name: debounce
notes:
- No `leading` or `trailing` option. Only a trailing debounce is supported.
- No `maxWait` option. The function may be debounced indefinitely if called frequently enough.
- The `pending` method is renamed to `isPending`.

name: difference
notes:
- Renamed to `diff`.
- Requires two arrays exactly. No more, no less.
- Supports an “identity function” that enables comparison through a property or other computation.

name: filter
notes: - “Collection” polymorphism is unaligned with Radashi's vision.

name: flatten
notes: - Renamed to `flat`.

name: flattenDeep
notes: - Use `Array.prototype.flat` instead.

name: flow
notes:
- Renamed to `chain`.
- Full type safety with TypeScript (to a max of 10 functions).
- Instead of taking an array of functions, each function is an argument to `chain`.

name: forEach
notes: - “Collection” polymorphism is unaligned with Radashi's vision.

name: get
notes: - “Key arrays” are not supported. Only string-based JSON paths.

name: groupBy
notes:
- Renamed to `group`.
- Property shorthand not supported (but coming soon).

name: isBoolean
notes: - Boxed values (e.g. `new Boolean(true)`) are not supported.

name: isEmpty
notes: - There are likely quite a bit of differences here. [Help wanted](https://github.com/radashi-org/radashi/issues/85) on this!

name: isNumber
notes: - Boxed numbers (e.g. `new Number(0)`) are not supported.

name: isObject
notes:
- Returns `false` for RegExp, Date, and other built-in, complex objects.
- Returns `false` for arrays.
- Returns `false` for functions.

name: isPlainObject
notes:
- Returns `false` for built-in namespaces like `Math`, `JSON`, etc.
- Returns `false` for the `arguments` object of a `function` call.

name: isString
notes: - Boxed strings (e.g. `new String("foo")`) are not supported.

name: kebabCase
notes: - Renamed to `dash`.

name: keys
notes:
- Use `Object.keys` instead.
- Radashi has its own `keys` function that is unrelated to Lodash `keys`.

name: map
notes: - “Collection” polymorphism is unaligned with Radashi's vision.

name: memoize
notes:
- Built-in support for TTL (time to live) invalidation.- By default, the cache key is computed with `JSON.stringify` of the arguments array. Lodash only uses the first argument if a custom key resolver is not provided.
- Lodash uses a `Map` to support any type of cache key, while only JSON-compatible arguments are supported in Radashi.
- No `cache` property, so the cache is not directly accessible.

name: merge
notes: - Radashi has a [`merge`](/reference/array/merge) function, but it's for merging two arrays based on a key function.

name: once
notes: - Support for clearing the cached result to allow running the function again. See the `once.reset` function.

name: padEnd
notes: - Use [`String.prototype.padEnd`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String/padEnd) instead.

name: pick
notes:
- Exactly one array of keys must be passed. No more, no less.
- You may pass a selector function instead (`pickBy` functionality).

name: pickBy
notes: - Renamed to `pick`.

name: reduce
notes: - “Collection” polymorphism is unaligned with Radashi's vision.

name: set
notes: - “Key arrays” are not supported. Only string-based JSON paths.

name: snakeCase
notes: - Renamed to `snake`.

name: some
notes: - “Collection” polymorphism is unaligned with Radashi's vision.

name: startCase
notes: - Renamed to `title`.

name: throttle
notes:
- No `leading` or `trailing` option. Only a trailing behavior is supported.
- The `pending` method is renamed to `isThrottled`.
- No `cancel` or `flush` method.

name: uniq
notes: - Renamed to `unique`.

name: uniqBy
notes: - Renamed to `unique`.

name: values
notes: - Use `Object.values` instead.
